correctness.rationale: A geometric H-fixed barycentric point has constant coefficients on full translation cosets; their uniform barycenters span the fixed complex iff the union of cosets is a Rips clique. A coset is allowable precisely when max_{h in H} wt(h)<=3, and two cosets are adjacent iff max_h wt(x+y+h)<=3. Counting each active coordinate in 2^(r-1) codewords bounds support and eliminates ranks >=4 by explicit rank-4 hyperplane weight-4 contradiction. At rank3 support size five would yield six pairwise-intersecting edges in K5, impossible (max four), leaving support three or four. Rank2 XOR weights classify exactly four forms; direct quotient Cayley generators give cube graphs for the first three and 4-cycles for the fourth. Rank3 quotient Cayley graphs are discrete; no triangles remain in the admissible orbit graphs, so graph models are exact PL homeomorphism types. Independently enumerated every rank>=2 subgroup of n<=5, checked coset adjacency and graph isomorphism for 155 admissible groups, and confirmed no extra rank>=4 cases; the unbounded result rests on the subgroup classification, not finite tests.

value.rationale: Simultaneous subgroup geometric fixed sets encode genuine equivariant information not contained in ambient homology or its representation character. The exhaustive sharp code-weight threshold and transition between connected cubes, many circular components and isolated points is a natural structural PL classification with explicit boundary cases.

final_claim: For n>=2 and linear translation H<=F2^n of rank r>=2, geometric fixed points in inclusive Hamming scale-three Rips are empty if max Hamming weight in H is >=4; if r=2 and max<=3 they form the 1D cube graph Q_(n-2) for nonzero weight multisets {1,1,2},{1,2,3},{2,2,2}, or 2^(n-4) disjoint circles for {2,3,3}; if r=3 and max<=3 they are 2^(n-3) isolated points; r>=4 cannot satisfy max<=3.
